definitions.explanation: A three-dimensional shape with six rectangular faces, like a box or brick.

examples.japanese: この{箱|はこ}は{直方体|ちょくほうたい}の{形|かたち}をしている。
examples.english: This box has the shape of a rectangular solid.

examples.japanese: {直方体|ちょくほうたい}の{体積|たいせき}は{縦|たて}×{横|よこ}×{高|たか}さで{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: The volume of a cuboid can be found by length × width × height.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{算数|さんすう}では{直方体|ちょくほうたい}と{立方体|りっぽうたい}の{違|ちが}いを{学|まな}び、{展開図|てんかいず}を{描|か}く{練習|れんしゅう}をする。
examples.english: In elementary school math, students learn the difference between cuboids and cubes, and practice drawing net diagrams.

notes:
A mathematical term used from elementary school onward. A {直方体|ちょくほうたい} has six faces that are all rectangles, with opposite faces being identical. A {立方体|りっぽうたい} (cube) is a special case where all edges are equal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {直方体|ちょくほうたい}の{体積|たいせき}: volume of a cuboid
- {直方体|ちょくほうたい}の{表面積|ひょうめんせき}: surface area of a cuboid
- {直方体|ちょくほうたい}の{展開図|てんかいず}: net of a cuboid

RELATED WORDS:
- {立方体|りっぽうたい}: cube (all faces are squares)
- {四角柱|しかくちゅう}: rectangular prism
- {円柱|えんちゅう}: cylinder
- {三角柱|さんかくちゅう}: triangular prism
